intro: Market data, definitions of the role, practical guides to agentic engineering, transition advice and the sceptical view. Each source has the two or three points that matter for this plan. The themes at the top summarise them and link to the sources behind each one.

sources.title: LinkedIn Jobs on the Rise 2026: The fastest-growing roles in Europe
keyPoints: AI Engineer (also titled Machine Learning Engineer) is first in the UK ranking; Head of AI is also on the UK list.
Most common UK AI Engineer skills: large language models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and NLP.
Most UK AI Engineer jobs are in London, Manchester and Cambridge.

sources.title: UK AI hiring and wages surge as they outpace jobs market: PwC AI Jobs Barometer
keyPoints: UK postings for specialist AI roles rose about 61% in 2025 (112k to 180k), while overall UK vacancies fell 6.6%.
The average UK wage premium for AI skills reached 34.2%, up from 11% the year before (the global figure is 62%).
Technology, media and telecoms, financial services and professional services have the highest shares of AI-related hiring.

sources.title: Indeed's 2026 Mid-Year UK Jobs & Hiring Trends Report
sources.author: Jack Kennedy
keyPoints: 9.4% of UK postings mentioned AI or AI tools at the end of June 2026, a new high.
Data and analytics has the highest AI-mention share of any category, at 48.8% of postings.
Graduate postings were down about 7% year on year, the lowest for the time of year since 2020.

sources.title: Four Takeaways from the 2026 Stanford AI Index
keyPoints: AI skills appear in 2.5% of US job postings, up 55% in a year.
Agentic AI skills rose from 0.06% to 0.23% of postings between 2024 and 2025, more than 280% growth and nearly 90,000 US postings.
Deployment skills (AWS, scalability, workflow management) have grown fastest over the long term; Python is the top specialised skill.

sources.title: The Future of Jobs Report 2025
keyPoints: Big data specialists, fintech engineers and AI and machine learning specialists are the fastest-growing jobs in percentage terms.
AI and big data top the fastest-growing skills.
Two-thirds of employers plan to hire for specific AI skills, while 40% expect to cut staff where AI can automate tasks.

sources.title: No Widespread Displacement, but the AI Employment Gap for Young Workers Has Widened to 19%
sources.author: Erik Brynjolfsson, Bharat Chandar, Ruyu Chen
keyPoints: Employment for 22 to 25 year-olds in highly AI-exposed occupations is about 19% below its counterfactual; experienced workers show no comparable gap.
Declines are concentrated where AI automates tasks. Where it complements workers, employment is flat or rising.
The adjustment comes mainly through less hiring of young workers, not layoffs. The patterns are descriptive, not causal (US payroll data).

sources.title: Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey Reveals Trust in AI at an All Time Low
keyPoints: 84% of developers use or plan to use AI tools, up from 76% in 2024.
46% don't trust the accuracy of AI output (31% the year before); 45% find debugging AI-generated code time-consuming.
Only 31% currently use AI agents.

sources.title: The Rise of the AI Engineer
sources.author: swyx (Shawn Wang)
keyPoints: The founding essay: foundation models and APIs created an engineering discipline that builds AI products without training models.
Shipping AI products needs engineers more than researchers; ML credentials aren't required.
Code orchestrates and extends LLMs, and AI will increasingly write that code too.

sources.title: AI Engineering: Building Applications with Foundation Models
sources.author: Chip Huyen
keyPoints: Defines AI engineering as building applications on existing foundation models, as distinct from traditional ML engineering.
Covers prompting, RAG, fine-tuning, agents, dataset engineering, latency, cost and model selection.
Puts heavy weight on evaluating open-ended outputs, including AI as a judge.

sources.title: Vibe coding is passé. Karpathy has a new name for the future of software.
keyPoints: Reports Andrej Karpathy's proposal to replace 'vibe coding' with 'agentic engineering'.
'Agentic' because the default is now orchestrating agents rather than writing code; 'engineering' because it's a learnable expertise.
Implies more oversight and scrutiny than vibe coding.

sources.title: Writing about Agentic Engineering Patterns
sources.author: Simon Willison
keyPoints: Agentic engineering: professional engineers using coding agents that write and execute code to amplify their existing expertise.
Initial working code now costs almost nothing, which changes how individuals and teams work.
Recommends red/green TDD: writing the tests first makes agents produce shorter, more reliable code.

sources.title: The future of agentic coding: conductors to orchestrators
sources.author: Addy Osmani
keyPoints: The engineer moves from implementer to manager: coder, then conductor, then orchestrator of several agents.
Writing specifications (design notes, acceptance criteria, definition of done) becomes a core skill.
'Trust, but verify': people stay accountable for reviewing agent PRs, tests, monitoring and security scanning.

sources.title: AI Evals: Everything You Need to Know
sources.author: Hamel Husain, Shreya Shankar
keyPoints: Start with error analysis (read traces, build a failure taxonomy) before building eval infrastructure.
Prefer binary pass/fail judgements to 1-5 scales.
Automate only the failures that persist, and validate LLM judges against human labels (TPR/TNR on held-out data).

sources.title: From Software Engineer to AI Engineer, with Janvi Kalra
sources.author: Gergely Orosz
keyPoints: Build LLM side projects; moving into an AI team internally is often easier than applying from outside.
AI engineer interviews mix algorithms, system design, take-home LLM apps and deep dives into LLM concepts.
The roles blend data science, front end, back end and product; be ready to throw work away when models improve.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.author: Erik Schluntz, Barry Zhang
keyPoints: Use the simplest solution, and add agentic complexity only when it measurably helps: it costs latency and money.
Start with LLM APIs directly; frameworks can hide prompts and make debugging harder.
Invest in the agent-computer interface: clear tool docs, testing how the model uses each tool, tools that are hard to misuse.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
sources.author: Prithvi Rajasekaran, Ethan Dixon, Carly Ryan, Jeremy Hadfield
keyPoints: Context engineering is curating everything the model sees: tools, history and external data, not just the prompt.
Context is finite and suffers 'context rot'; aim for the smallest set of high-signal tokens.
For long tasks: compaction, structured notes, sub-agents and just-in-time retrieval.

sources.title: Writing effective tools for agents — with agents
sources.author: Ken Aizawa
keyPoints: Tools are a contract between deterministic systems and non-deterministic agents; design for agents, not as thin API wrappers.
Namespace tools and return compact, high-signal responses with pagination, filtering and actionable errors.
Improve tools with evaluations on realistic multi-step tasks, including using Claude Code to refine them.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.author: Mikaela Grace, Jeremy Hadfield, Rodrigo Olivares, Jiri De Jonghe
keyPoints: Combine code-based graders, model-based graders calibrated against people, and human review.
pass@k (at least one success in k) suits tools; pass^k (all k succeed) suits customer-facing reliability.
'20-50 simple tasks drawn from real failures is a great start.'

sources.title: Best practices for Claude Code
keyPoints: The most important practice: give the agent a check it can run (tests, build, linter) so it can verify its own work.
Keep CLAUDE.md short: commands, non-default rules, test instructions and gotchas. Move occasional workflows into on-demand skills.
Explore, plan, then code. Manage context aggressively; use headless mode in CI and review sub-agents.

sources.title: Manage costs effectively (Claude Code)
keyPoints: Token costs scale with context size; the docs give an enterprise average of about $13 per developer per active day.
Levers: clear context between tasks, pick the right model and effort, pre-filter logs and test output with hooks, keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines.
Prompt-cache statistics and OpenTelemetry export make per-user cost observable; agent teams use several times the tokens of a single session.

sources.title: Claude Code GitHub Actions
keyPoints: Runs Claude Code in CI: @claude mentions implement fixes, issues become PRs, and runs can be scheduled or event-triggered.
Automated PR review posts inline comments; CLAUDE.md defines the review criteria.
Cost and safety controls: max turns, timeouts, concurrency limits, least-privilege permissions, an allowed-tools list and human review before merge.

sources.title: OpenAI co-founds the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation
keyPoints: The foundation launched with OpenAI's AGENTS.md, Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Block's goose as founding projects.
AGENTS.md is an open 'README for agents': build and test commands, style, security and PR rules.
It's supported by Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI and others, so instruction files are becoming a cross-tool standard.

sources.title: Copilot code review now runs on an agentic architecture
keyPoints: Copilot code review now calls tools to gather wider repository context, which GitHub says gives better, less noisy comments.
Runs on GitHub Actions runners; generally available on paid plans.
Reads repository instruction files, including AGENTS.md.

sources.title: 2026 Agentic Coding Trends Report
keyPoints: Core claim: software development is shifting from writing code to orchestrating agents that write it.
Trends include multi-agent teams, long-running agents and human oversight.
Engineering value moves towards architecture, agent coordination, quality evaluation and breaking problems down. (Vendor report.)

sources.title: Exclusive: SRA authorises first AI-only law firm
keyPoints: The SRA authorised Garfield.Law, an AI-driven small-claims debt recovery firm, the first in England and Wales.
Named solicitors stay accountable; the regulator checked quality controls, confidentiality and conflict safeguards.
A UK example of demand for people who combine legal or regulatory understanding with AI system design and supervision.

sources.title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
sources.author: Joel Becker, Nate Rush, Tom Cunningham, David Rein, Khalid Mahamud
keyPoints: METR's early-2025 trial found experienced open-source developers were 19% slower with AI while believing they were about 20% faster.
A late-2025 follow-up estimated an 18% speed-up for returning developers and 4% for new ones; both confidence intervals include no effect.
Many developers withheld tasks they didn't want to do without AI, so METR treats the design as unreliable and the estimate as a likely lower bound.

sources.title: Google DORA Research: Software Developers Use AI 'Heavily'
keyPoints: About 90% of roughly 5,000 DORA respondents use AI at work, around two hours a day.
AI is an amplifier: it magnifies the strengths of high-performing organisations and the dysfunctions of struggling ones.
Throughput rises, but making sure software works before release is still hard, so testing and platform foundations come first.

sources.title: AI-Generated Code Poses Major Security Risks in Nearly Half of All Development Tasks
keyPoints: Across 80 tasks and 100+ LLMs, generated code contained OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities in 45% of cases.
Java failed more than 70% of the time; Python, C# and JavaScript 38-45%.
Security hasn't improved even as models write more syntactically correct code. (Vendor-run study.)

themes.theme: AI Engineer is the fastest-growing role, defined by LLM, RAG and NLP skills
themes.evidence: LinkedIn puts AI Engineer first in the UK for 2026, with London, Manchester and Cambridge as hubs; the WEF lists AI and ML specialists among the fastest-growing jobs worldwide.

themes.theme: UK AI demand and pay are rising while the wider market cools
themes.evidence: UK specialist AI postings rose 61% in 2025, with a 34.2% wage premium, while overall vacancies fell 6.6%. Almost half of UK data and analytics postings now mention AI.

themes.theme: The work is moving from training models to building systems on top of them
themes.evidence: AI engineering means building on existing foundation models. Value moves to architecture, agent coordination, evaluation and breaking problems down, and 'agentic engineering' is the new professional label.

themes.theme: Agentic AI skills are a fast-emerging hiring signal
themes.evidence: Agentic AI skills grew more than 280% in US postings between 2024 and 2025, to nearly 90,000 postings.

themes.theme: Context, instruction files and token budgets are now a craft
themes.evidence: Context is finite and degrades as it fills. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md encode a repository's rules, AGENTS.md is now a Linux Foundation standard, and agent cost scales directly with context size and caching.

themes.theme: Evals and verification loops set people apart, and they reward statistical skill
themes.evidence: Recommended practice: error analysis, binary judges validated against people, and 20-50 tasks from real failures. Claude Code's top best practice is to give the agent a check it can run.

themes.theme: Automated review and agents that fix CI are becoming standard
themes.evidence: Copilot code review became agentic in March 2026 and reads AGENTS.md. Claude Code GitHub Actions reviews PRs against CLAUDE.md and implements fixes, with turn and permission limits.

themes.theme: Designing tools and MCP servers for agents is its own skill
themes.evidence: Agent tools need namespacing, compact outputs and eval-driven iteration. MCP is now a Linux Foundation project, and the agent-computer interface deserves as much care as the prompt.

themes.theme: Production and deployment skills still matter, and they transfer from MLOps
themes.evidence: Deployment skills have grown fastest over the long term, and DORA finds AI only helps teams with strong engineering foundations.

themes.theme: Judgement, security and accountability are scarce, and experience is protected
themes.evidence: Trust in AI output is falling, 45% of generated code had OWASP flaws, and measured speed-ups are uncertain. Job losses fall on young workers, while experienced people in AI-complemented roles hold steady.

caveats: No strong, independent dataset shows UK data scientist or 'deploy and maintain ML' roles shrinking. The evidence shows these roles being retitled and expected to use AI, so I frame it as the role changing, not collapsing.
PwC's 2026 figures (s2) were read from summaries because the page blocks automated access; check them on the page before quoting.
The Karpathy framing (s10) comes from secondary coverage of a social media post.
Anthropic, GitHub, OpenAI and Veracode are vendors with commercial interests in what they publish.
The Stanford and Lightcast data (s4, s6) are US-based and descriptive, not causal.
The productivity evidence is mixed: METR's intervals include zero, and DORA and Stack Overflow are self-reported surveys.
Product docs (s19-s21) are living pages without a fixed date; they were read in October 2026.
